name: Berdazimer gel
lead: Berdazimer gel, sold as Zelsuvmi, is a prescription topical medicine that releases nitric oxide onto the skin to clear molluscum contagiosum, the small, dome-shaped bumps caused by a poxvirus. By clearing these visible lesions, it helps restore smooth, even-looking skin, particularly for children and for adults whose bumps are conspicuous.[2][4]

The FDA authorized Zelsuvmi on January 5, 2024 for people aged one year and older; it is described as the first licensed prescription medication for molluscum that is applied at home.[4] It is applied once daily to lesions for up to 12 weeks and is supplied as two components, a berdazimer gel and a hydrogel, that are combined for use.[4]

Efficacy was examined in vehicle-controlled phase 3 trials, including the 891-participant B-SIMPLE4 study, and in a meta-analysis of four randomized trials with 1,854 patients.[6][2] The most common side effects are local: burning, itching, redness and irritation at the application site.[4]

angle.text: Berdazimer gel is applied daily to molluscum bumps, and in trials a larger share of treated participants reached complete clearance than with vehicle gel. Clearing the bumps removes a visible skin-texture concern, and the trials also tracked scarring.

paras: Berdazimer gel is indicated for molluscum contagiosum in patients aged one year and older.[4] The condition is a common viral skin infection, mostly in children, with lesions that can last months to years and may cause itching, self-consciousness and household spread.[5][12]

In the phase 3 B-SIMPLE4 trial, 891 participants aged six months and older with 3 to 70 lesions applied berdazimer 10.3% gel or vehicle gel once daily for 12 weeks; the primary endpoint was complete clearance at week 12.[6][13] A meta-analysis of randomized trials found berdazimer effective for lesion clearance and reported reduced scarring, while noting a higher rate of topical adverse effects that matters particularly for children.[2]

An integrated analysis of three randomized trials, a trial in people with atopic dermatitis, a pharmacokinetic study and a Japanese open-label study have also been published.[8][7][10][11] A systematic review of molluscum treatments describes berdazimer's safety profile as favorable for pediatric patients, and a review on adherence notes that daily topical treatments face adherence challenges.[1][3]

The gel generates nitric oxide, which has antiviral properties; the exact mechanism in molluscum is described as unclear but thought to involve inflammation, immune regulation and viral replication.[4] Laboratory work has examined its effect on the molluscum virus in vitro.[9]
Reported effects are mostly at the application site, including burning, itching, redness and irritation.[4]

timeline.event: Phase 3 B-SIMPLE1 and B-SIMPLE2 trials begin.[15][14]
FDA authorizes Zelsuvmi for molluscum in people aged one year and older.[4]

card.summary: A prescription nitric oxide gel that clears molluscum bumps, leaving smoother skin.
card.note: Prescription only; local burning and itching are common.

quick.overview:
Berdazimer gel (Zelsuvmi) is a prescription gel for molluscum contagiosum, the small raised bumps caused by a virus. Applied once daily to the lesions for up to 12 weeks, it releases nitric oxide.

People use it to clear the bumps and return the skin to a smooth, even look. It was FDA authorized in January 2024 for ages one and up.
quick.mechanism: The gel releases nitric oxide on the skin, which has antiviral properties. The exact way it clears molluscum is described as not fully understood.
quick.risks: The most common effects are burning, itching, redness and irritation where it is applied. It is available by prescription in the US.
